# J&J beats earnings estimates; Middle East conflict weighs on medical device sales

By [Michael Erman](https://www.reuters.com/authors/michael-erman/)

October 13, 2026 10:21 AM UTC Updated 33 mins ago

People gather next to a logo of Johnson & Johnson at the company’s booth at the 8th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, China, November 6, 2025.REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/china-international-import-expo-in-shanghai/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX1JDMlVRSEFLRU5DWQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Tremfya sales jump 68%, topping estimates
*   CFO says Middle East conflict, European austerity and China pricing pressures weighed on device sales

Oct 13 (Reuters) - Johnson & Johnson [(JNJ.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/JNJ.N) reported a slightly higher-than-expected ​profit on Tuesday, driven by strong sales of immune disease treatment Tremfya, but ‌geopolitical issues including the Middle East conflict were a drag on its medical devices business.

The company posted third-quarter revenue of $25.4 billion, above analysts' average estimate of $25.28 billion, according to LSEG data. Adjusted earnings of $2.59 ​per share also topped Wall Street expectations of $2.54.

Pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% in the ​quarter to $16.76 billion. Medical technology division sales rose only 2.5% to $8.6 billion ⁠overall. Outside the US, sales in the division were basically flat.

J&J Chief Financial Officer ​Joe Wolk, in an interview, said the [Mideast conflict](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/), austerity measures in Europe and pricing in China ​continued to weigh on results internationally, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way."

He said the Mideast conflict, which has led to soaring fuel costs at home and abroad, has yet to impact the company's costs, but ​has hurt sales in the region.

"These are countries that still value and actually want ​premium healthcare systems, think Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia. They pride themselves on having solid healthcare, very good ‌healthcare," Wolk ⁠said. "But their budgets now are being resourced and allocated towards defense."

Sales at its Abiomed heart pump business also remained slow after a UK study earlier this year [raised questions](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/jj-quarterly-earnings-beat-wall-street-estimates-strength-medicines-unit-2026-07-15/) about the use of Impella pumps during certain high-risk coronary procedures.

Tremfya sales rose 68% to $2.4 billion, exceeding ​analyst estimates of ​about $2.19 billion, while sales ⁠of Stelara, which is facing generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Tremfya has increasingly replaced ​lost Stelara revenue following recent approvals in inflammatory bowel diseases.

Sales of ​blood cancer ⁠treatment Darzalex rose about 16% to $4.24 billion, short of analyst expectations of $4.4 billion.

The company raised its full-year forecast for reported sales to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, from $101.1 billion previously. It ⁠increased its ​adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 ​per share, up from $11.04.

J&J shares closed at $263.73 on Monday. They have risen 27% this year, outperforming both the broader ​market and most healthcare peers.

Reporting by Michael Erman in New York; Editing by Bill Berkrot
